External Reviewer Report Guidelines The External Report (ER) is submitted by the external consultants to the Dean/Chair within three weeks of the site visit. The report should address the following: ● Executive Summary ● Introduction of reviewers and their roles ● Dates of the visit ● Consultant’s summary of strengths and challenges as identified in the Self-Study Report ● Consultant’s summary of strengths and challenges observed during the visit and not identified in the Self-Study Report ● Recommendations for how the department can expand on its strengths and address its challenges ● Additional information reviewer(s) deem relevant to address departmental goals 37

Requesting Funds for External Reviewers Note: Booking travel may be done by the reviewer themselves where they also pay themselves or by the department. Either way reimbursement will be made. The Provost Office will cover a $1,250 honorarium/stipend for up to two reviewers, as well as travel expenses (airfare, hotel, per diem, parking). However, we do not cover any meals with faculty members. If faculty are paying out of pocket for shared meals, then that would need to be reimbursed out of other department funds (this is not covered by the Provost’s Office). An expense breakdown should be included with a request for funding. If you are using department funds for the travel authorizations (TA's) then this expense breakdown is used as backup. The department gives an estimate of total expenses with complete information prior to the visit. SECTION 4. ACTION PLAN 39

Overview of the Action Plan The Action Plan outlines the strategic plan of the Department for the next six years including annual benchmarks used to assess progress. The plan addresses major issues raised in the self- study and by the external reviewer(s), and relates these to the strategic plan of the Department. The plan also includes specific goals, their rationale, and estimates of resources required. ● Faculty review and discuss the external reviewer’s self-study, and the Department Chair collaborates with the faculty to develop a draft Action Plan that is submitted to the Dean. ● The Dean meets with the Department chair (and/or the self-study chair, if a different person) to develop a mutually agreeable proposed Action Plan that is submitted to the Provost with the Self-Study and the External Reviewer Report. ● The Department chair, the Dean, the Provost and representatives from the Provost’s office meet to discuss the Action Plan for the Department which outlines the strategic plan for the next six years, addressing any major issues raised in the self-study and external review, and includes specific goals and resource estimates. ● To promote continuous quality improvement, the Provost may request a follow up, Interim Report from the department. Interim reports will be submitted to the Dean who will present them to the Provost for discussion. ● The approved Action Plan is complete following this discussion and represents an agreement between the Department, the college Dean, and the Provost for actions to be taken over time, benchmarks used to assess progress, and a plan for allocation of resources. 40

Action Plan Guidelines Action Plan Development, Milestones and Implementation Plan Action Planning is a continuous and multi-year process. See the table below for a detailed timeline of milestones associated with Action Plan Development and Implementation. Timeline Activity Description Initial Development Year 1, Months 1-3 Faculty Engagement Faculty review and discuss the findings from the external review and the self-study, kickstarting the development of the Action Plan. Year 1, Months 4-6 Drafting the Plan The Department Chair collaborates with faculty to create a draft Action Plan. This draft is then submitted to the Dean for initial feedback. Review and Approval Process Year 1, Months 7-9 Collaborative Refinement The Dean and the Department Chair (including the self-study chair if different) refine the draft Action Plan into a mutually agreeable proposal. Year 1, Month 10 Strategic Submission This proposed Action Plan, together with the Self-Study and the External Reviewer Report, is submitted to the Provost for preliminary approval. Year 1, Months 11-12 Comprehensive Discussion The Department Chair, Dean, Provost, and representatives from the Provost’s office meet to discuss, finalize, and approve the Action Plan. Implementation and Monitoring Year 2-5 Action The approved Action Plan is implemented, 41

Implementation setting the course for the department’s actions. Departments initiate projects and strategies outlined in the plan and start monitoring their impact. Year 2-5 Regular Monitoring Departments conduct annual reviews to monitor progress against the benchmarks set in the Action Plan. Adjustments are made based on these reviews to ensure the plan remains responsive to both achievements and challenges. Goals and progress toward goals are discussed annually with the Dean. Year 6 Evaluation and Preparation for Next Cycle A comprehensive evaluation of the Action Plan’s outcomes is conducted to assess its effectiveness and gather insights for the next APR cycle. This evaluation informs the upcoming self-study and the development of a new Action Plan. Cycle Repeats Year 6, Months 1-3 Start New Cycle The next cycle begins with updated orientation and data collection, reflecting the latest developments and priorities in the department’s discipline and the broader institutional context. 42

Preparing for your meeting with the Office of the Provost 1) Email your APR, External Review Report and completed Action Plan to the Provost and Executive Vice President for Academic Affairs, the Vice Provost for Academic and Faculty Initiatives and the Provost’s executive assistant. 2) Create a one-pager to help guide the 1-hour conversation with the Provost’s Office. 1.Engaged Attendance:Presence at the monthly Senate meetings is essential,asa
quorum is needed to conduct our business.You are the voice of your colleagues,and
for equitable engagement,and helps build community,it is also possible to attend
remotely.Agendas and any supporting materials are distributed in advance of each
meeting,along with details on how to connect online.Attendance at any special events
is equally important(for example,a Senate-sponsored forum for the general faculty on
a specified topic)

Who may attend Faculty Senate meetings and where are they held?
Any member of the URl community or the general public may attend a Faculty Senate
meeting.However,only voting members of the Senate may vote on legislation,resolutions,
officer elections,and any other business raised at the meeting.Bylaws stipulate that only
Senators and ex officio members have the RIGHT to speak during meetings.Exofficio
members participate in discussions,ask questions,and make and second motions;theyare
not,however,allowed tovote.Non-senators may request to speak at a meeting beforehand
via the online Permission To Speak”form found on the Faculty Senate website.To facilitate
the meeting itself
Meetings take place throughout the academic year in the Hope Roomof the Higgins
Welcome Center from3-5p.m.monthly on a Thursday.A brief reception with refreshments is
provided at every meeting.This is a wonderful opportunity for in-person attendees to network
colleges
How are agenda items determined?
The meeting agenda is set by the Faculty Senate Executive Committee.Agenda items may
can also be suggested to the Executive Committee via an anonymous form on the Faculty

can also be suggested by a committee or introduced at a Senate meeting during the New
Business'portion.
While agenda items maybe suggested at anytime,inclusion of an item at the monthly
meeting requires the Executive Committee approve adding it to the agenda atleast one week
in advance of the scheduled senate meeting.This is necessary for timely agenda posting and
motion in realtime are typically considered for inclusion on a future agenda or referred to a
standing or special committee for further exploration.Exceptions to this timeline are reserved
for unusually urgent or time-sensitive Issues.
Doesthe Faculty Senate use parliamentary procedures to conduct meetings?
The Senate relies upon the American Institute of Parliamentarians Standard Codeof
Parliamentary Procedure.Guidebooks and other reference materials are available in the
Faculty Senate Office.Training on procedural basics is provided during the annual
Orientation meeting.This meeting is held each September and is required for all new
Senators(and highly recommended as a refresher for ALL Senators).
